description: Kataglyphis shared Renovate preset. Adopt with: { "extends": ["github>Kataglyphis/ANTfrastructure"] }

It lives at the repository ROOT as default.json because that is the only filename `github>Kataglyphis/ANTfrastructure` resolves to (a preset under .github/ would need the explicit `github>Kataglyphis/ANTfrastructure:<name>` form).
Renovate reads it from ANTfrastructure's DEFAULT BRANCH, including for ANTfrastructure itself, so a change here only reaches any consumer - or the hub - once it is merged.

The consumers currently carry Dependabot configs that have never opened a PR; this preset is what replaces them, and the reason it exists as a preset rather than four copies is that the git-submodules line below is the part everyone forgets.

Renovate DISABLES the git-submodules manager by default, which is why every Kataglyphis submodule gitlink - ANTfrastructure's own third_party/DocumANTation pin included - has been unwatched since the day it was added. Nothing else in this preset matters as much as this one line.
The manager bumps a gitlink to the tip of the branch named in .gitmodules (falling back to the remote's default branch), so a submodule that wants to be watched needs a `branch = <name>` entry there.

Owner rule 2026-10-07 (bleeding edge): every lockfile moves to the newest release its manifest allows, not only the entries a manifest edit touches. Without this, an in-range release never appears in any report: WebDavClient's uv.lock sat 41 packages behind, DocumANTation's 19 and OmniAccelerANT's pubspec.lock 17 while every manager said up to date.

Under --platform=local Renovate builds this update but never reports it, so renovate-local.sh carries it itself: its report lists each maintained lock, and --apply runs the lock tool's upgrade command. See docs/dependency-updates.md#lock-file-maintenance
`at any time`: the local CLI runs on demand and never reads a schedule, and Renovate's own default (before 4am on monday) would only hold back a bot that is not installed.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions pin bumps are low-risk; group them into one PR instead of one per action.

description: Composite actions resolved at @develop are a deliberate exception to digest pinning: a consumer workflow that pinned ANTfrastructure's own actions to a SHA would stop picking up the upstream-first change flow the repos are built around (upstream is pushed BEFORE the consumer change that needs it).
This rule only stops Renovate from proposing those pins; workflows keep pinning every THIRD-PARTY action by digest.

packageRules.description: A submodule bump moves a whole dependent repository, so it gets its own PR and its own label rather than being folded into a group.

description: A pubspec's `environment: flutter:` floor (`>=3.41.6`) is a range, but the flutter-version datasource defaults to exact semver, so Renovate skipped every such floor as invalid-value and never looked it up (NOT CHECKED in OmniAccelerANT's 2026-10-07 report). npm versioning reads the range the way pub does.
Moved here from OmniAccelerANT's own config on 2026-10-07, so every Flutter consumer (ANThology, jotrockenmitlocken) gets it.
CMake dependencies named by a GitHub URL: GIT_REPOSITORY followed by GIT_TAG, or a tag archive URL. Renovate has no CMake manager. See docs/dependency-updates.md#cmake-dependencies
Only a dotted value is a version: a branch (master) or a commit SHA is skipped, and a comment between the URL and GIT_TAG leaves the pin to the annotated form below, so no pin is reported twice.

CMake pins too irregular for the URL forms: a `# renovate: datasource=<ds> depName=<dep> [extractVersion=<re>] [versioning=<v>]` line, and on the very next line `GIT_TAG <v>`, `set(<NAME> <v>` or a quoted "<v>". See docs/dependency-updates.md#cmake-dependencies
